ranked_facts.why: The brain MRI showing T2/FLAIR hyperintensity in the right basal ganglia and internal capsule with mild surrounding edema is more consistent with an infectious process, such as viral or bacterial meningitis, than with an inflammatory condition like autoimmune encephalitis.

The presence of a high white blood cell count in the cerebrospinal fluid, along with elevated protein and decreased glucose, is more indicative of a bacterial or viral infection than a neoplastic process.

The elevated opening pressure, high WBC count, elevated protein, and low glucose in the cerebrospinal fluid are more consistent with an infectious process, such as bacterial meningitis, than with an inflammatory condition like autoimmune encephalitis.

The progression of the lesion with new involvement of the left basal ganglia, increased diffusion restriction, development of necrosis, and new peripheral contrast enhancement on the repeat MRI is more suggestive of an infectious or inflammatory process rather than a vascular event like a stroke.
